payload.origin: dev-team tick 2026-07-21T17:07Z, Step 0a-D. Router found a NEW signal_queue row aged 36h, formed two wrong hypotheses about why, disproved both against the source, and landed on this one.
payload.envelope_note: Enveloped with from/to/type so this file drains instead of pinning the inbox floor.

finding.title: cowork-addressed signal_queue rows are not being marked READ on WORK ticks — a row has sat NEW for 36h while the gate that counts it provably forces WORK every tick
finding.owner_suggestion: po triage. Router did NOT mint a board row, did not mark any row READ, and did not touch the cowork flow.
evidence_chain: 1. Row po-20260720T052606 (from=po, to=unified-agent, type=methodology-flag) has status=NEW with ts=2026-07-20T05:26:06Z — 36h+ old at time of writing.

2. scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh Step 7 (lines 243-252, read verbatim) computes signal_count over .signal_queue.rows[] where status==NEW AND .to is in [po, tran-ngoc-bau, unified-agent, alert-commander]. unified-agent IS in that list, so this row is counted.

3. The SILENT branch fires ONLY if slots_empty AND one_shots_empty AND signal_count -eq 0. With this row NEW, signal_count >= 1 continuously since 2026-07-20T05:26Z, so NO cowork tick since then can have returned SILENT — every one must have emitted WORK.

4. docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/main.md WORK-continuation step 1 mandates: 'the script only did a READ-ONLY count for the SILENT gate (R4); run the real drain-and-route-and-mark-READ body of Step 0a below'. So the mark-READ body is required on every one of those ticks.

5. cowork demonstrably ticked today: task_list_held shows published:market-watcher-eod:2026-07-21 claimed 16:13Z, published:news-scout-offhours:2026-07-21 at 16:15Z, published:market-watcher-offhours:2026-07-21 at 16:17Z — all owner_client_session 9f4a6bfc-b001-4349-8a44-545f24c1b0ac. Slots fired, so the dispatcher ran.
6. The row is still NEW. Conclusion: the drain-and-mark-READ body did not execute on those WORK ticks, even though the slot-dispatch half of the same tick did.
finding.second_consequence_cost: signal_count is now permanently >= 1 (3 NEW rows, all cowork-addressed), so the SILENT gate can never fire. The preflight script's own header states the SILENT path covers ~80% of ticks and exists so no LLM read is needed. Every cowork tick — every 15 minutes — now takes the WORK path and burns a full LLM read regardless of whether any slot is due. The optimization is fully defeated for as long as any cowork-addressed row sits NEW, which is exactly the condition this defect creates. It is self-sustaining.
finding.saturated_gate_pattern: This is the SECOND saturated threshold found in this single tick. The other: the drain guard in docs/agents/dev-team/flow/drain-signals.md fires on 'ls docs/signals/*.json | wc -l > 50', and the inbox has a permanent structural floor of 54 undrainable files (46 cowork-team state files, 7 price_anomaly, 1 outage) — so that predicate also fires every tick regardless of state and can no longer detect a genuine new accumulation. Same shape both times: a threshold whose input has a floor above it stops discriminating while still reporting that it fired. Worth a sweep for other count-threshold gates with pinned inputs rather than fixing these two in isolation.
hypotheses_router_formed_and_DISPROVED: DISPROVED — 'unified-agent has no signal_queue drain, so the row is undeliverable by design.' False: cowork-team Step 0a explicitly drains to in [po, tran-ngoc-bau, unified-agent, alert-commander] on behalf of its members. Routing is correct.

DISPROVED — 'the row arrived during a quiet period and SILENT ticks skip the drain.' False in the direction assumed: the SILENT gate counts NEW cowork-addressed rows precisely so this cannot happen. The gate is correctly designed; something downstream of it is not running.
finding.residual_uncertainty_do_not_skip: Router did NOT determine WHICH failure mode this is, and the distinction changes the fix. Candidates: (a) the WORK-continuation drain body is narrated but not executed — there is an existing memory for exactly this failure shape in cowork (feedback_cowork_spawn_narrates_not_executes); (b) the drain ran and the mark-READ write failed or was lost to a CAS race; (c) the drain is skipped when the tick's slot work is non-empty, i.e. slots crowd out step 1. Whoever picks this up should determine which BEFORE changing anything — (a) is a flow-compliance problem, (b) is a write-path problem, (c) is an ordering problem, and a fix aimed at the wrong one will look green and change nothing.

payload.router_did_not: mark any signal_queue row READ, mint a board row, edit the cowork flow or its preflight script, or spawn cowork-team.
